abstract: Competing speech can cause excess emissions in a connectionist temporal classification (CTC) recognizer. We penalize the amount by which the noisy student's expected collapsed token count exceeds a frozen teacher's count on the paired clean utterance. The one-sided objective caches one scalar per utterance and adds no inference module. With 147,456 trainable parameters in wav2vec 2.0, it improves competing-speech word error rate (WER) over matched CTC-only adaptation across three development seeds. On a locked LibriSpeech test, speech-interference WER falls from 45.198% to 44.323%, while clean WER changes by 0.004 percentage points. Unseen VCTK interferers yield a 0.307-point improvement. Ablations favor collapsed-count control over frame-mass regularization. Longer training increases the speech gain but worsens noise and music performance, identifying an insertion-deletion tradeoff rather than uniform robustness.

oneSentenceThesis: 本文针对竞争语音导致 CTC 识别器多吐词的问题，用冻结模型在配对干净语音上的期望折叠词元数作锚，只惩罚混合语音学生的超出部分，在 147456 参数的早期层适配下降低语音干扰词错误率，但长训练会在噪声和音乐上以删除增加为代价。
originalTitle: Clean-anchored excess-emission control for CTC adaptation under competing speech
